# Is a Local LLM Smart Enough, and How Do You Tell Whether It Works for Your Company? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB06

# Is a Local LLM Smart Enough, and How Do You Tell Whether It Works for Your Company?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/is-local-llm-good-enough/)

The short answer

Public leaderboards cannot answer this; test with your own questions. Prepare 30 to 50 questions employees really ask, each with a correct answer, and run the local model and a cloud model on the same company documents, comparing accuracy and speed question by question. Rule out configuration problems before testing: Ollama's default context is only 4,096 tokens, and when retrieved passages do not fit, the model looks "dumb".

## 1. Why leaderboards are not enough

Leaderboards measure general ability. Your company needs answers from your documents, in your language, to your questions. OpenAI's evaluation best practices say the same: design task-specific evals that reflect real-world usage. Anti-patterns it lists include relying only on generic academic metrics, test data that does not match production traffic, and treating "it seems to work" as a pass.

So the question is not "which model is stronger" but "on our 50 questions, how many does it get right, where does it fail, and what does each failure cost?"

## 2. Three configuration reasons a local model seems "dumb"

Before concluding anything, rule out problems unrelated to model ability:

- Context too short for the documents.  Ollama's default context is 4,096 tokens. When AI searches company documents, retrieved passages go into the context; what does not fit is cut off, and the model answers from incomplete material. Raise it with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH  or num_ctx , at the cost of more memory (see "What hardware does a local LLM need?").

- Model not fully on the GPU.  If the PROCESSOR column in ollama ps  shows a CPU/GPU split, part of the model runs on the CPU and responses slow down noticeably. That is a speed problem, not an intelligence problem, but it is often mistaken for "local models don't work".

- Reasoning settings left at default.  Some models let you set reasoning effort; OpenAI's gpt-oss accepts low, medium, or high in the system prompt. Testing multi-step questions at low effort is not a fair test.

## 3. A five-step comparison test

- Collect questions.  Pick 30 to 50 from what employees actually ask, customer service logs, and internal email. Include three kinds: answerable from the documents; not in the documents, where the AI should say it doesn't know or hand off; and questions the user has no permission to see.

- Write correct answers and sources.  For each question, record the answer and which passage of which document it comes from.

- Run both under the same conditions.  Same documents, same retrieval settings, same questions for the local and cloud models.

- Score question by question.  Use four categories (correct, partly correct, wrong, answered when it should have declined) and record response time. Where it fails matters more than the total.

- Set the threshold in advance.  For example, a required share of correct answers on answerable questions, and zero made-up answers on questions that should be declined. Adopt only if met. When you change models or settings later, rerun the same set.

The usual outcome is not "all local" or "all cloud" but a split: which work goes to the local model, and which work, where the data allows, uses the cloud-assisted version.

Brand information | Think BIG

## How Think BIG decides whether a model is good enough

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real Co., Ltd.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- Acceptance by test questions, not demos : people who know the business write test questions, correct sources, and acceptable answer ranges; each retrieved passage and final answer is checked, including cases the AI cannot answer and permission boundaries.

- Re-verify after changing models : when a model is changed, the workflow and output quality are re-verified, and whether existing settings still apply is decided by test results.

- Pre-delivery security review : before each system is delivered, its code and configuration go through a security review; if it does not pass, it is not delivered.

See [RAG knowledge Q&A](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/rag/) and [AI Agent acceptance framework](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/ai-acceptance/).

The actual scope of Think BIG's services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: How far behind cloud models like ChatGPT are local models? It depends on the task; public leaderboards cannot answer it for your company. Run 30 to 50 real company questions on both, with the same documents and settings, and compare accuracy and speed question by question. Q2: Why does a local model answer poorly when reading company documents? Often the context is too short. Ollama's default context is 4,096 tokens, so retrieved passages that do not fit are cut off. You can raise the context, but memory use goes up. Q3: How many questions are needed to test a local model? About 30 to 50, covering questions answerable from documents, questions the AI should decline or hand off, and questions the user has no permission to see, each with a correct answer and source. Q4: After switching to a new local model, do we need to test again? Yes. After any model or setting change, rerun the same test set and confirm accuracy and declining behavior have not regressed before going live.

Sources (checked 2026-10-19)

- Ollama FAQ (default context 4096, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH and num_ctx, CPU/GPU split in ollama ps): [docs.ollama.com](https://docs.ollama.com/faq)

- OpenAI gpt-oss-120b model card (reasoning levels low/medium/high): [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b)

# What Hardware Does a Company Need to Run a Local LLM, and How Much GPU Memory? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB02

# What Hardware Does a Company Need to Run a Local LLM, and How Much GPU Memory?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/local-llm-hardware-sizing/)

The short answer

Start with GPU memory, not the CPU. The model file must fit entirely in GPU memory, with room left for context and the number of people using it at once. Going by download sizes in Ollama's official library, an 8B-class model is about 5.2GB, 14B about 9.3GB, and 32B about 20GB. OpenAI states that gpt-oss-20b can run within 16GB of memory, while gpt-oss-120b fits on a single 80GB GPU.

## 1. Why GPU memory comes first

To answer a question, a local model has to be loaded into memory. Whatever fits in GPU memory runs on the GPU; whatever does not is placed in system memory and computed by the CPU, which is noticeably slower.

Ollama's ollama ps  shows the split directly. A PROCESSOR value of 100% GPU  means the whole model is on the graphics card; a ratio such as 48%/52% CPU/GPU  means only part of it fits (the example in Ollama's FAQ). So the order is: decide the model size, check whether GPU memory is enough, then look at everything else.

## 2. How much space common models need

Download sizes from Ollama's official library (default tags, checked 2026-10-19). File size roughly equals the memory needed to load the model; context needs additional memory on top.

Model
Download size
Context length
Official note
qwen3:8b
5.2GB
40K
—

qwen3:14b
9.3GB
40K
—

qwen3:30b (MoE, 30B-A3B)
19GB
256K
Mixture of experts; only part of the parameters are active per step

qwen3:32b
20GB
40K
—

gpt-oss:20b
14GB
128K
Official: runs within 16GB of memory

gpt-oss:120b
65GB
128K
Official: fits on a single 80GB GPU

Hardware reference points (official figures):

- Consumer graphics card example: the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 has 32GB of GDDR7 memory, enough for every model above up to 32B.

- Desktop AI system example: NVIDIA DGX Spark has 128GB of unified memory; NVIDIA states a single unit runs models up to 200 billion parameters.

Prices and availability in Taiwan change quickly, so this page lists none; check current quotes from resellers.

## 3. Four steps to choose hardware

1. Decide the task, then the model.  Answering from company documents, organizing data, and drafting replies usually work with mid-sized models. There is no need to start with a machine for the largest model. To judge whether a model is good enough, see "Is a local model smart enough?"

2. Size GPU memory from the model file, with headroom.  Ollama's default context is 4,096 tokens. Letting the AI read more document passages at once means raising the context, which uses more memory.

3. Count concurrent users separately.  Ollama's FAQ states that OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL  sets how many requests each model handles at once, and required memory scales with parallel requests times context length. When memory runs short, new requests queue. Ten people asking at once need more memory than one.

4. Place and configure the machine properly.  An AI Agent that must respond at any time needs a machine that stays on 24 hours. Ollama binds to 127.0.0.1 port 11434 by default; if you open it to the office network, use a firewall to allow only specific devices, and do not expose it to the internet.

Brand information | Think BIG

## How Think BIG helps companies choose hardware for local models

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real Co., Ltd.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- Check existing equipment first : we look at whether current computers can do the job before suggesting any purchase.

- Verify with real work, not just specs : before delivery we confirm which hardware the model actually uses (for example, whether the GPU is really running) and test response speed with the company's real questions.

- Pre-delivery security review : before each system is delivered, its code and configuration go through a security review; if it does not pass, it is not delivered.

The actual scope of Think BIG's services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: For a local LLM, does the CPU or the graphics card matter more? Start with GPU memory. When the whole model fits, the GPU does the work; whatever does not fit goes to the CPU and slows things down noticeably. With Ollama, the PROCESSOR column in `ollama ps` shows the split. Q2: What can run on 16GB of GPU memory? By Ollama's official library sizes, 8B-class (about 5.2GB) and 14B-class (about 9.3GB) models fit. OpenAI also states that gpt-oss-20b runs within 16GB of memory. Leave room for context. Q3: How much memory if many staff use it at once? Calculate it separately. Ollama's FAQ states that required memory scales with the number of parallel requests times context length, and new requests queue when memory runs short. Q4: Can the local model machine be exposed to the internet? Not recommended. Ollama binds only to 127.0.0.1 by default. To let other office devices use it, open access to specific devices through a firewall rather than to the internet.

Sources (checked 2026-10-19)

- Ollama FAQ (CPU/GPU split in ollama ps, default context 4096, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL and memory, default binding 127.0.0.1:11434): [docs.ollama.com](https://docs.ollama.com/faq)

- Ollama library, qwen3 (download sizes and context): [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/library/qwen3)

- Ollama library, gpt-oss (download sizes, 16GB and single 80GB GPU): [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/library/gpt-oss)

- OpenAI gpt-oss on GitHub (117B/21B parameters, MXFP4, hardware): [github.com](https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss)

# Can a Local LLM Work Offline, and How Do You Update Models and Software in an Air-Gapped Environment? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB08

# Can a Local LLM Work Offline, and How Do You Update Models and Software in an Air-Gapped Environment?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/offline-local-llm-updates/)

The short answer

Yes. After a model is downloaded to the machine, answering questions needs no network. Truly offline operation takes three things: turning off cloud features (Ollama supports OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 ), not applying automatic updates directly (Ollama on macOS and Windows downloads updates automatically), and changing updates to "download, verify, and test on a connected machine, then move into the offline environment and install".

## 1. What needs a network

Using Ollama as the example (checked against official documentation on 2026-10-19):

Action
Network needed?
Notes
Answering with a downloaded model
No
Ollama states that when you run locally, it does not see your prompts or data

Downloading models (ollama pull )
Yes
Ollama FAQ: Ollama pulls models from the internet and may require a proxy

Software updates
Yes
macOS and Windows download updates automatically, applied via "Restart to update"; on Linux, rerun the install script

Cloud models and web search
Yes
Unavailable once cloud features are disabled

Other tools an AI Agent uses (web search, email, LINE) need a network by nature. For an offline environment, decide first whether to remove them or allow them only to specific destinations.

## 2. Offline settings checklist

- Turn off cloud features.  Set OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 , or set disable_ollama_cloud  in ~/.ollama/server.json . After a restart, the log shows Ollama cloud disabled: true .

- Pin the version; do not apply auto-updates directly.  Record the current version. Leave "Restart to update" alone until an update has been tested.

- Serve only on the machine or the internal network.  Ollama binds to 127.0.0.1  port 11434 by default. To let other internal devices connect, open access to specific devices through a firewall.

- Set the model location.  Use OLLAMA_MODELS  to set the model directory for easier backup, transfer, and control.

- Test with the network actually cut.  With outbound connections blocked at the firewall, confirm Q&A still works and check connection logs for any unexpected outbound traffic.

## 3. Five steps for offline updates

- Download on a connected test machine.  Get the new software and model files on a separate test machine.

- Verify source and hashes.  OWASP's supply chain guidance: use only models from verifiable sources and check integrity with signing and file hashes.

- Run the same test questions.  After a model or version change, rerun the company's fixed test set to confirm answer quality has not regressed (see "Is a local LLM smart enough?").

- Move it in on approved media.  Models can be imported as GGUF: create a Modelfile  with FROM /path/to/file.gguf , then run ollama create model-name . Ollama's documentation notes it does not quantize GGUF files on import, so prepare the quantized file in advance.

- Record versions and keep the old one.  Note versions, dates, and test results before and after; keep the previous version so you can roll back.

Brand information | Think BIG

## How Think BIG's on-premises version handles connectivity and updates

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real Co., Ltd.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- External connections confirmed one by one : on-premises does not mean every connection stays local; if cloud models, messaging apps, or other external services are used, those requests still go to that service, and we confirm each one before building.

- Pinned versions, no auto-updates : skills and packages are scanned before installation, pinned, and not auto-updated; updates are verified before they go in.

- Changes can be rolled back : before any change, scope, reason, owner, and rollback method are confirmed, and the change runs only after approval within the authorized scope.

See [On-premises AI and data sovereignty](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/) and [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/).

## FAQ

Q1: Can Ollama run completely offline? Yes. Once a model is downloaded, answering needs no network. To keep it from reaching the cloud, set `OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1` or `disable_ollama_cloud` in server.json; the trade-off is losing cloud models and web search. Q2: How do you install a new model without internet? Download the GGUF model file on a connected machine and check its hash, move it to the offline machine, create a Modelfile with `FROM /path/to/file.gguf`, and run `ollama create`. Q3: Does Ollama update itself? Per the official FAQ, the macOS and Windows versions download updates automatically and apply them when you choose "Restart to update"; on Linux you rerun the install script. For production, pin the version and update only after testing. Q4: How do you confirm a local model makes no outbound connections? Run a real Q&A test with outbound connections blocked at the firewall, and check connection logs for any unexpected outbound traffic.

# Can Open Models Be Used Commercially? Four License Checks Before a Company Adopts One | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Local LLMs
TB12

# Can Open Models Be Used Commercially? Four License Checks Before a Company Adopts One

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/open-model-license-checklist/)

The short answer

Not always. It depends on the license of the exact version you download, not on the model's reputation or the word "open". Before adopting one, check four things: whether the license allows commercial use, whether there is a user-count or revenue threshold, whether there is an acceptable use policy (a list of prohibited uses), and what conditions apply to derivative models and redistribution. Versions within the same model family can carry different licenses.

## 1. "Open" does not mean "anything goes"

In everyday use, "open-source model" usually means a model whose weights you can download and run on your own hardware; "open-weight" is the more precise term. Being downloadable does not mean there are no conditions. The conditions are in the license file that comes with each model.

Licenses fall roughly into two groups:

- General permissive open-source licenses , such as the Apache License 2.0: they grant royalty-free rights to reproduce, prepare derivative works, and distribute. Redistribution requires including a copy of the license, marking modified files as changed, and retaining existing copyright and license notices.

- Licenses or terms written by the model provider : these may add user-scale thresholds, prohibited uses, attribution rules, or naming rules for derivative models.

So the answer to "can we use it commercially?" always comes from the official license text for that version.

## 2. Four checks before adoption

Check
What to look for
Why it matters
1. Commercial use allowed
Whether the grant is restricted to research or non-commercial use
Some models allow only research or personal use

2. User-count or revenue threshold
Above what number of users or revenue a separate license is required
Most small and mid-sized companies will not reach it, but confirm whether it exists and where it sits

3. Acceptable use policy
The prohibited-use list, and whether it is a condition of the license
Breaching a prohibited use can mean breaching the license

4. Derivative models and redistribution
How fine-tuned models must be named, whether attribution is required, what must accompany distribution
Installing a model in a system delivered to a customer may count as redistribution

Read each model's official license page yourself: find the license file (usually LICENSE) on the model's official download page or repository and match it to the version number you actually downloaded.

## 3. Record licenses in the component inventory

OWASP's supply chain guidance for LLM applications (LLM03:2025) recommends inventorying all license types involved with a bill of materials (BOM) and keeping an up-to-date software bill of materials (SBOM). In practice, for each system you should be able to look up:

- Which model, which version, and where it was downloaded from.

- The license name for that version and a copy of the license file.

- The licenses of the tools and packages that run the model, recorded separately from the model license.

- The result of the four checks, with who confirmed it and when.

When a model is updated, read the new version's license again. Licensing involves legal judgment; before commercial use, have legal counsel confirm against your actual use.

Brand information | Think BIG

- Models can be changed : when a model is changed, the workflow and output quality are re-verified, and whether existing settings still apply is decided by test results.

See [Enterprise](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/) and [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/).

## FAQ

Q1: Can all open-source models be used commercially for free? Not always. Being able to download the weights does not mean there are no conditions. Check the license of the exact version: some allow only research use, and some have user-scale thresholds or prohibited-use lists. Q2: How do you confirm whether a model can be used commercially? Find the license file on the model's official download page or repository, match it to the version you downloaded, and check four points: commercial use, user-count or revenue thresholds, acceptable use policy, and derivative and redistribution conditions. Q3: Can a fine-tuned model be sold or delivered to customers? It depends on the original license's terms for derivative models and redistribution, such as naming rules, attribution requirements, and documents that must accompany distribution. Installing a model in a system delivered to a customer may count as redistribution. Q4: How should a company manage the model licenses it uses? Record model, version, download source, license file, and check results in the component inventory (SBOM), record tool and package licenses separately, and recheck when models are updated. Have legal counsel confirm before commercial use.

# What Is Prompt Injection, and Can Documents or Web Pages an AI Agent Reads Give It Instructions? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Enterprise AI Security
TB04

# What Is Prompt Injection, and Can Documents or Web Pages an AI Agent Reads Give It Instructions?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/prompt-injection-ai-agent/)

The short answer

Yes. Prompt injection hides instructions in content the AI will read so that it does something it should not. When the instructions sit in outside content such as web pages, documents, or résumés, it is called indirect prompt injection. OWASP lists it as LLM01 in its 2025 Top 10 for large language model applications and states it is unclear whether fool-proof prevention exists. So the goal for a company is that even if the AI is fooled, it cannot do anything dangerous.

## 1. How prompt injection happens

OWASP's definition: a prompt injection occurs when input alters the model's behavior or output in unintended ways. There are two kinds:

- Direct prompt injection : the user types input meant to make the AI break its rules.

- Indirect prompt injection : the AI takes in content from an outside source (a website or file) that contains hidden instructions, and treats them as commands. These can be invisible to people, such as white text on a white background.

OWASP's scenarios include: an AI asked to summarize a web page whose hidden instructions cause it to leak the private conversation; a résumé uploaded with malicious instructions split across sections, which manipulate the model's evaluation of the candidate; and an attacker modifying a document in a RAG knowledge base to change the AI's answers.

Why AI Agents need more care than chat AI:  a fooled chatbot says something wrong; a fooled AI Agent that can send email, query data, or edit files may actually act.

How it differs from jailbreaking:  OWASP notes the terms are often used interchangeably. Jailbreaking is a form of prompt injection aimed at making the model ignore its safety rules; prompt injection is broader and covers any input that alters the model's behavior.

## 2. Five defenses a company can put in place

OWASP's recommendations, in a form companies can apply:

- Separate outside content from instructions.  Web pages, emails, and attachments the AI reads are marked as data, not instructions. The system prompt states the AI's role and limits.

- Least privilege.  An AI Agent that reads outside email does not get permission to send email or delete files. Sensitive functions are handled in code, not left to the model.

- Human approval for high-risk actions.  Sending externally, spending money, deleting, or changing production data happens only after a person confirms. Even if the AI is fooled, it stops at that gate.

- Check output formats in code.  Define the expected output format and validate it with deterministic code; anything that does not match is blocked.

- Run adversarial tests regularly.  Treat the model as an untrusted user and test whether trust boundaries hold.

OWASP also notes that RAG and fine-tuning make answers more relevant and accurate, but research shows they do not fully mitigate prompt injection. The defenses have to come from permissions and process, not the model alone.

## 3. A quick self-check

Ask your provider or your IT team:

- Which content written by others does this AI Agent read? (Web pages, customer emails, uploaded files, shared documents)

- After reading it, what actions can it take? (Send email, change data, pay, call external services)

- Which actions always pause for a person to confirm?

Anything that both reads outside content and can act directly, with no human check in between, is the first thing to fix.

Brand information | Think BIG

## How Think BIG reduces the impact of prompt injection

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real Co., Ltd.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- Least privilege : for each AI Agent we confirm data sources, read/write scope, and access roles under the principle of least privilege.

- Human approval : external sending, spending, and changes to production systems are decided by a designated person. AI Agents provide work output and evidence; people keep the key decisions.

- Pre-delivery security review : before each system is delivered, its code and configuration go through a security review; if it does not pass, it is not delivered. No one can promise perfect security; what we do is review, one gate at a time.

See [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/) and [Enterprise](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/).

The actual scope of Think BIG's services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: What is indirect prompt injection? The AI takes in content from an outside source such as a web page or file, and hidden instructions in that content get treated as commands. The instructions may be invisible to people. Q2: How is prompt injection different from jailbreaking? OWASP notes the terms are often used interchangeably. Jailbreaking is a form of prompt injection aimed at making the model ignore its safety rules; prompt injection is broader and covers any input that alters the model's behavior. Q3: Can RAG or fine-tuning prevent prompt injection? Not fully. OWASP states that RAG and fine-tuning improve relevance and accuracy, but research shows they do not fully mitigate prompt injection. Q4: How can a company defend against prompt injection? Separate outside content from instructions, give AI Agents least privilege, require human approval for high-risk actions, validate output formats in code, and run adversarial tests regularly. The goal is that a fooled AI still cannot do anything dangerous.

- OWASP GenAI Security Project, LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency (least privilege, human approval): [genai.owasp.org](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/)

# When AI Searches Company Documents, How Do You Make Sure Each Department Sees Only Its Own Data? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Building AI Agents
TB10

# When AI Searches Company Documents, How Do You Make Sure Each Department Sees Only Its Own Data?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/rag-access-control-by-department/)

The short answer

Enforce permissions at the retrieval step, not by relying on the AI's judgment. When indexing, tag each document with its department and the roles allowed to read it. When an employee asks a question, the system searches only documents that person may see, so restricted passages never reach the AI. Then verify with test questions for content the user must not see, confirming neither the answer nor the citations expose it.

## 1. Why "don't reveal this" in the prompt is not enough

In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the system first finds relevant passages and then hands them to the model to write the answer. Once a restricted passage is retrieved and placed in the model's context, the model has seen it. Asking it through the prompt not to repeat it is unreliable: the model can make mistakes or be steered by prompt injection.

OWASP's 2025 Top 10 for LLM Applications lists this as LLM08, Vector and Embedding Weaknesses: inadequate or misaligned access controls can allow unauthorized access to embeddings containing sensitive information, and when multiple classes of users share one vector database, context can leak between users or queries. OWASP recommends fine-grained access controls with permission-aware vector and embedding stores, and strict logical and access partitioning of datasets.

## 2. Four steps

- Inventory documents and tag permissions.  Record each document's owner, current version, department, and allowed roles. Documents without permission tags stay out of the knowledge base.

- Store permissions with the index.  Each chunk carries the permission tags of its source document. Highly sensitive data, such as HR and payroll, can go into a separate knowledge base.

- Filter before retrieval.  Based on the person asking, search only the scope they may see. The system makes the authorization decision, not the model. OWASP LLM06 calls this complete mediation: enforce authorization in downstream systems instead of relying on the model.

- Verify with must-not-see tests.  For example, have a regular employee account ask about a rule only managers may see, and confirm neither the answer nor the citations expose it.

## 3. Three common gaps

Gap
How it happens
How to close it
Citations leak
The answer does not say it, but the attached source link or excerpt exposes restricted content
Apply the same permissions to citations

Permissions out of sync
An employee changes department or leaves; the file system is updated, but the knowledge base tags are not
Sync permissions from a single source and spot-check regularly

Withdrawn document still indexed
An old rule is withdrawn but its passages remain in the index, so the AI answers by the old rule
Update the index when withdrawing documents and log it as a change

Brand information | Think BIG

## How Think BIG handles knowledge base permissions

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real Co., Ltd.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- Readable scope checked before retrieval : the asker's identity and document permissions are checked first, then relevant passages are retrieved from approved documents. Permissions are enforced at retrieval, not only by telling the prompt "don't reveal".

- Permissions applied to citations too : readable scope is checked by role, and neither answers nor citations may expose restricted content.

- Acceptance includes permission boundaries : we confirm unauthorized users are blocked, and retest after documents are withdrawn or the index is updated.

See [RAG knowledge Q&A](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/rag/) and [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/).

The actual scope of Think BIG's services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: Can an AI knowledge base have department-level permissions? Yes. Tag each passage with department and allowed roles when indexing, and search only the scope the asker may see, so restricted passages never reach the AI. Q2: Is telling the AI in the prompt not to reveal secrets enough? No. Once a restricted passage is retrieved into the context, the model has seen it and may reveal it by mistake or under prompt injection. The system must block it at retrieval. Q3: Is it safe for several departments to share one vector database? Only with access control. OWASP LLM08:2025 warns that when multiple user groups share a vector database, data can leak between users, and recommends permission-aware stores with strict partitioning. Q4: How do you confirm permissions actually work? Use must-not-see tests: have an account without permission ask about restricted content and confirm neither the answer nor the citations expose it. Test again after staff changes and document withdrawals.

# When AI Searches Company Documents, Where Does the Data Go in Cloud vs. On-Premises Setups? | Q&A Library | Think BIG

[← Q&A Library](https://thinkbigtw.com/en/qa/)

Enterprise AI Security
TB03

# When AI Searches Company Documents, Where Does the Data Go in Cloud vs. On-Premises Setups?

Think BIG Q&A Library  ·  2026-10-19
      ·  [中文](https://thinkbigtw.com/library/qa/rag-data-flow-cloud-vs-local/)

The short answer

On-premises: employees' questions, company documents, and the AI's answers are all processed on the company's own hardware. Cloud-assisted: the employee's question, plus the document passages the system retrieves, are sent to the model provider and retained for a period under the provider's rules (for example, up to 30 days by default for the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs). One more check: if the embedding step used for indexing also runs on a cloud service, document content is sent out in chunks when the index is built.

## 1. The four stages data passes through

The common way to let AI search company documents is RAG (retrieval-augmented generation): before answering, the AI retrieves relevant passages from company documents and writes the answer from them. The approach comes from Lewis et al. (2020). Data passes four stages:

Stage
What happens
On-premises
Cloud-assisted
1. Indexing
Documents are split and converted to vectors in a knowledge base
On company hardware
Depends: a local embedding model keeps it in-house; a cloud embedding API sends the passages out

2. Retrieval
Relevant passages are found for the question
On company hardware
Usually on company hardware or a server under the company's account

3. Answering
"Question + retrieved passages" go to the model
Model on company hardware
Question and passages go to the model provider

4. Logging
Chat logs, system logs, backups
Stored where the company designates
The company keeps its own logs; the provider retains data under its own policy

Stage 3 is the key. The cloud-assisted version does not send the whole knowledge base, but every question sends the passages retrieved for it. More questions mean more document fragments leave the company.

## 2. How long providers retain data

Per official documentation (checked 2026-10-19):

- OpenAI API : since March 1, 2023, API data is not used for training by default. Abuse monitoring logs, which may include prompts and responses, are retained up to 30 days by default. Eligible customers can apply for Zero Data Retention, subject to OpenAI's prior approval.

- Anthropic API : inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days of receipt or generation by default. Exceptions include customer-controlled storage (such as the Files API), separate agreements, Usage Policy enforcement, and legal requirements.

So the cloud-assisted version means two things: data leaves the company, and it stays on someone else's servers for a while. If a policy says a document must never leave the company, it belongs only in the on-premises knowledge base.

## 3. Five questions to ask before you start

- Where does embedding happen?  A local model or a cloud API? With a cloud API, document content leaves when the index is built.

- Where is the answering model?  Local or a cloud provider? Under whose account?

- Where are chat logs and system logs kept, and for how long?  Who can see them?

- What other external services are connected?  LINE, email, cloud storage: messages through any of these pass through that service.

- Which documents must never leave?  List them and confirm they only go into the on-premises knowledge base.

If all five have clear answers, the data flow is understood. Any question without an answer is where to dig further.

Brand information | Think BIG

## Think BIG's two deployment options

Think BIG (Think BIG Make it Real Co., Ltd.) is an enterprise AI Agent deployment provider headquartered in Taiwan. Starting from protecting company data, we build AI Agents inside the client's own environment (company hardware, or a cloud server under the company's account). There are two deployment options: with the on-premises version, models and documents are processed on company hardware; with the cloud-assisted version, employees' questions and the document passages the system retrieves are sent to the model provider for processing.

- External channels confirmed one by one : on-premises does not mean every connection stays local. If an external channel such as LINE is added, messages through that channel pass through that service; we list this for the client before building.

- API accounts under the company's name : with the cloud-assisted version, the company applies for the model API under its own account, under the provider's terms, so billing and usage records stay with the company.

- Data flow listed before building : where the application, model, knowledge-base index, source documents, logs, and backups each sit is listed item by item. Permissions are enforced at retrieval, not only through prompts.

See [RAG knowledge Q&A](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/rag/), [On-premises AI and data sovereignty](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/), and [Trust](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/).

The actual scope of Think BIG's services follows what both parties confirm.

## FAQ

Q1: Does using a cloud model to search company documents send the whole knowledge base? No, but each question sends the employee's question and the passages retrieved for it to the model provider. If the indexing step uses a cloud embedding API, document content is also sent in chunks when the index is built. Q2: Does on-premises deployment mean no data ever leaves? Not necessarily. On-premises decides where the model and documents sit. If the workflow connects to a cloud model, messaging app, or other external service, that part of the data goes out. Check the local model, outbound restrictions, logs, and backups. Q3: How long do cloud model providers keep the data I send? Per official documentation, OpenAI API abuse monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days by default; Anthropic API inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days by default, with exceptions. Actual terms depend on your plan and contract. Q4: What should we ask before letting AI search company documents? Where embedding happens, where the answering model runs, where logs are kept and for how long, which external services are connected, and which documents must never leave the company.

Sources (checked 2026-10-19)

- Lewis et al. (2020), Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

- OpenAI API, Your data (no training by default, abuse logs up to 30 days, Zero Data Retention by approval): [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/your-data)

- Anthropic Privacy Center, How long do you store my organization's data? (30-day deletion and exceptions): [privacy.claude.com](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866-how-long-do-you-store-my-organization-s-data)

- OpenAI, Embeddings guide (embedding text via the API): [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/embeddings)

- Think BIG, RAG knowledge Q&A (data flow; cloud text conversion and indexing services count as data flow): [thinkbigtw.com](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/rag/)

Two channels, one foundation

## Two ways customers find you — both need to work

Today's customers find you in two very different ways. Both rely on the same underlying foundation, so doing them separately is wasteful — doing them together is efficient.

### Channel 1: Google Search (SEO)

When a customer types your industry and location into Google, where do you rank?

- How many of your pages Google has indexed, which important pages are missing

- Mobile usability, page speed, and technical architecture issues

- Title tags, descriptions, and structured data correctness

- Local search and Google Business Profile completeness

- Where you currently rank for the keywords your customers actually search

### Channel 2: AI Answers (GEO)

A growing share of customers ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI directly: "Which company in this category is recommended?"

- Whether 5 major AI platforms mention you, and how they describe you

- Which sources the AI cites, and how competitors compare

- Whether the AI has described you incorrectly (wrong address, missing services, confusion with another brand)

- Whether the AI answered from training memory or actually retrieved your site

- Different AI platforms prefer entirely different sources — what works for one may not work for another

Both channels rely on the same foundation: a crawlable site, well-structured content, a consistent identity across platforms, and credible off-site mentions. We address all of this together — no duplicated work, no conflicting advice.

SEO vs GEO

Service phases

## Audit → Foundation Build → Monthly Management

The audit comes first. The foundation build is next. Monthly management is ongoing — not a subscription you can skip to.

1

SEO + GEO Visibility Audit

One-time · Prerequisite

Tells you exactly where you stand: a combined Google search status and AI mention baseline across five major platforms in one report, ending with a prioritized "do these three things first" list.

Google Search Audit deliverables (SEO):

- Index coverage:  how many pages Google has indexed, which important pages are missing (via site: query and Search Console if authorized)

- Technical foundation:  mobile usability, HTTPS, Core Web Vitals public data, sitemap/robots, duplicate URLs and canonicals, broken links

- 10 keyword positions:  where you currently rank on Google for searches your customers use, and who ranks above you (factual report only — no commentary on competitors)

- Page structure:  title tags, meta descriptions, H1, internal linking, and structured data (Schema) correctness

- Local search:  Google Business Profile completeness, map search ranking, review response status

AI Visibility Baseline deliverables (GEO):

- AI Visibility Baseline Report:  5 major AI platforms × 15–20 questions your customers would actually ask — each question logged for whether the AI mentioned you, how it described you, and which sources it cited

- Competitor mention comparison:  who the AI mentioned for the same questions, and how often (factual record only)

- Retrieval trigger log:  for each question, whether the AI answered from training memory or actually retrieved your site (two different gaps, two different fixes)

- Error and confusion inventory:  what the AI has gotten wrong about you — outdated address, missing services, confusion with a same-name company — each item sourced and ranked by priority

- Per-AI action list:  different AI platforms prefer entirely different source types, so your action list is broken down by platform, not given as a single universal prescription

- Methodology page:  which questions, which day, which AI version, how many repetitions — you can re-run the same queries and verify our numbers

- Compliant tactics only:  the report flags which approaches carry platform rule violations or legal risk in Taiwan, so you know what to avoid

For businesses without a website: we audit your Google Business Profile, marketplace listings, and social channels instead; the AI check works identically.

The report's final page combines SEO and GEO findings into a single prioritized "do these three things first" list. A debrief call is included after delivery.

2

Foundation Build Package

One-time · Includes audit

The next step after the audit: fix the SEO technical issues, restructure content so AI platforms are willing to cite it, and begin building credible off-site mentions. The right choice for anyone who wants to build the foundation correctly from the start.

SEO build items:

- Technical fix list (we implement what we can directly; for client-managed sites we provide an engineer-ready checklist)

- Title, description, and content revision recommendations for 10 keyword-matched pages

- Internal linking clean-up

- Google Business Profile optimization

- Sitemap submission and Search Console setup assistance

GEO build items:

- Content restructuring: answer-first writing, FAQ optimization, quotable fact statements

- Schema structured data implementation

- Entity consolidation: consistent name, sameAs links, directory registration

- First two off-site citable content pieces (government or trade directories, Google Business, Threads/YouTube long-form, named media submissions, review site listings — compliant channels only)

- Off-site roadmap document: per-AI-platform expansion directions for future months

For businesses without a website: the foundation build skips website changes and instead creates off-site content assets that AI platforms can cite.

3

Monthly Management and Monitoring

Ongoing · Three-month minimum

Ongoing work and reporting after the foundation is in place. Each month's deliverables include a combination of content production, off-site placement, and a monitoring report.

- Content written for AI citation:  answer-first, clearly stated facts, Q&A and list formats — structured so it works for both SEO (keyword relevance, headings, internal links) and GEO (quotable, answer-first) at the same time

- Off-site placement:  government and trade directories, Google Business Profile, named Threads/YouTube long-form content, named media submissions, review site listings — distributed across multiple channels, not concentrated in one

- Identity alignment:  company name, social links, and directory information kept consistent across all platforms

Monthly report includes:

- Google Search section:  keyword rank tracking, Search Console impressions and click trends (with client authorization), technical anomaly alerts

- AI Visibility section:  mention rate trend (repeated sampling over multiple days, with confidence intervals), competitor mention comparison, source gap recommendations

- Our own site as a live demonstration:  we run the same process on thinkbigtw.com from scratch and report our own relative changes each month — so what you see is someone actually doing the work, not just a slide deck

We do not commit to specific rankings or citation counts. What we commit to is: real repeated-sampling data with confidence intervals that hold up statistically — not a single query screenshot.

Methodology

## Why we measure this way

The measurement method determines whether a report is worth trusting. We publish the methodology because transparency is the core of this service.

### Repeated sampling, not a single query

Academic research (University of St. Gallen, 2026) has confirmed that re-running the same question on the same day yields citations with only a 32–43% overlap. AI citation is a probability distribution — a single query is statistically near-meaningless. We query each question across multiple days, then review results manually to derive a defensible range.

### Per-AI breakdown, not a universal list

Taiwan field data shows: Gemini tends to cite official websites and review directories; Perplexity favors Threads and YouTube discussions; ChatGPT favors government institution directories and cites non-Chinese sources 70% of the time. Cross-platform source overlap is only 5–20%. Your action list is broken down by AI platform.

### Confidence intervals, not single-point numbers

For a brand detection rate to have a standard error below 0.10, you need at least 7 repetitions on the same day and a rolling window of 10+ days. Our reports only make claims supported by statistical evidence: if confidence intervals overlap, we write "no meaningful change," not a fabricated improvement figure.

### Retrieval trigger rate: memory vs. live retrieval

57% of ChatGPT responses to queries don't trigger a web search at all — the model answers from training memory, meaning your website is invisible to it regardless of how good it is. We log the trigger status per question; the two gap types require entirely different fixes.

### Methodology you can verify yourself

Every report includes: which questions were asked, on which dates, with which AI version, how many repetitions, API or browser, and region settings. You can take the same questions and re-run them yourself to verify our numbers aren't fabricated.

### SEO measurement: index, technical, keywords, local

- Index: site: queries and Search Console index status

- Technical: Core Web Vitals public data, mobile, HTTPS, canonicals

- Keywords: Search Console or manual queries, factual current-state report only

- Local: Google Business Profile completeness, map ranking position

Google official references: [SEO Starter Guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/seo-starter-guide), [AI Features and Your Website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)

What we never do

## Our hard limits — stated plainly

These practices are available in the market. We don't use them — not because we can't, but because they harm you.

✕

### Buying clicks or traffic

Artificially inflating clicks or purchasing traffic violates [Google's spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) and can result in your site being penalized or removed. We don't do it and don't recommend it.

✕

### Buying links or building PBNs

Link buying and private blog networks are explicitly cited violations in Google's spam policies. They may produce short-term effects but carry serious long-term risk. We only build genuine, sustainable off-site presence.

✕

### Posting commercial content on forums that prohibit it

Forums like Dcard and PTT explicitly prohibit commercial promotion in their rules. Getting caught means deleted posts, account bans, and reputational damage. We only produce named, compliant off-site content.

✕

### Fake reviews, sock-puppet accounts, anonymous astroturfing

Taiwan's Fair Trade Act prohibits content written in a third-party voice to mislead consumers. Any paid recommendation we produce is disclosed. We don't write fake reviews or maintain fake accounts.

✕

### Manipulating AI answers (hidden text, prompt injection)

Google explicitly listed "manipulating AI-generated answers" in its [spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) in 2026. Hidden text and prompt injection can get your site penalized or removed. Our approach is to make content genuinely worth citing — not to deceive the system.

✕

### Promising specific rankings or citation counts

Rankings are decided by Google. AI citations are probability distributions. Anyone who tells you "you will be on page one" or "AI will definitely recommend you" is telling you what you want to hear. We give you real data, not empty promises.

Honest timeline

## How long does it take? The honest version.

SEO and GEO both accumulate over time — they are not on/off switches. The following reflects typical patterns; actual timelines vary by industry competitiveness, how much verifiable information you make available, and AI platform algorithm changes.

Weeks 4–8

After content and page structure adjustments, initial movement starts appearing in both Google search and AI visibility.

Months 5–6

AI platforms start citing you in answers; Google keyword rankings show meaningful movement.

Months 6–12

Search and AI presence becomes more established; citation count shows a clear upward trend.

Factors that influence speed: how competitive your industry is, how much quantifiable information you are willing to publish, whether you have an existing website to improve, and AI platform algorithm changes (an external variable we monitor continuously).
We do not promise specific rankings or dates  — but you will see real monthly data showing how your search and AI visibility is developing.

FAQ

## Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between SEO and GEO, and why do them together?

SEO is about being found when someone searches on Google. GEO is about being cited when someone asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, or a similar AI a question. Both rely on the same foundation: a crawlable site, well-structured content, consistent identity across platforms, and credible off-site mentions. Doing them separately means duplicated effort — we audit and prioritize both together in one pass.

I don't have a website. Can I still use this service?

Yes. For businesses without a website, we audit your Google Business Profile, marketplace listings, directories, and social channels instead. The AI visibility check works identically. For the foundation build, we create off-site content assets rather than modifying a website.

Can you get me to the first page of Google?

Rankings are determined by Google — no one can promise you a specific position. We do not buy clicks, traffic, or links; those violate [Google's spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies). What we commit to is doing the right work and providing verifiable monthly data so you can see your search and AI visibility develop over time.

How long before I see results?

SEO and GEO both accumulate — they are not on/off switches. In general: initial changes from content restructuring appear within 4–8 weeks; AI citations start to appear around months 5–6; noticeable presence growth comes around months 6–12. Actual timelines depend on industry competitiveness, how much verifiable information you publish, and AI platform algorithm changes. We do not commit to specific rankings or dates.

How do you measure AI visibility? Is it just a screenshot of one query?

No. We query five major AI platforms with 15–20 questions your customers would actually ask, repeated across multiple days. Academic research (University of St. Gallen, 2026) shows citation overlap between runs on the same question on the same day is only 32–43% — a single query is statistically near-meaningless. Our reports show a range with a confidence interval. Every report includes the full methodology — which questions, which day, which AI version, how many repetitions — so you can re-run the queries yourself and verify.

What do you never do?

We never buy clicks, traffic, or links; never create fake reviews or sock-puppet accounts; never post commercial content on forums that prohibit it; and never use hidden text or prompt injection to influence AI answers. Google explicitly listed AI answer manipulation in its spam policies in 2026. We build genuinely citable content — not gaming the system.

What do I need to provide to get started?

Three things: your industry, your brand name or URL (if you don't have a website, tell us where you sell), and the 3–5 competitors you care most about. We'll draft 15–20 questions your customers would actually ask an AI, share them with you first, then run the full check. For the Google search audit, Search Console read access makes the report significantly more complete — but it works without it too.

Is my information kept confidential?

Your brand information, competitor list, and any Search Console data you authorize us to read are used solely to produce your report. They are not used for other client research, not shared externally, and not used as marketing material. Client identities and cases are always kept confidential — we never name clients publicly. That is a baseline commitment.

and cited by AI?

Start with an audit. Know exactly where you stand — then decide the next step.

# AI Agent 職能組合｜企業協作與營運模型｜Think BIG

FUNCTIONAL AI AGENTS

# 以職能協作，
重塑工作流程。

依客服、業務、行銷、財務及維運職能配置 AI Agent，將資料輸入、交付產物與人工決策整合為明確的營運模型（Operating Model）。以下為可評估的能力範圍，非客戶案例。

客服 AI Agent 組合

## 以知識依據支援客服作業。

能力範圍 依核准知識整理問題、查找依據與準備回覆。

交付產物 附資料來源的回覆草稿、無法回答的問題清單。

人工決策與授權 資料沒有依據時交回人員；涉及承諾、退款或爭議的內容，由負責人決定。

企業知識問答如何準備依據？[了解 RAG、文件權限與回答驗收 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/rag/)

業務與客戶聯繫 AI Agent 組合

## 整合需求紀錄與聯繫追蹤。

能力範圍 整理詢問、聯絡理由與追蹤待辦，依流程準備聯繫草稿。

交付產物 詢問摘要、待聯繫清單與每筆工作的處理狀態。

人工決策與授權 先確認聯繫授權、管道規範與停止聯繫機制；不預設自動撥號或發送。

行銷 AI Agent 組合

## 建立一致的內容生產與覆核流程。

能力範圍 把核准的品牌資料整理成草稿，檢查內容與待補資訊。

交付產物 可編修的內容草稿、來源與發布前檢查清單。

人工決策與授權 發布、廣告投放與任何花費，保留人員核准。

財務 AI Agent 組合

## 強化資料彙整與差異核對。

能力範圍 依約定格式整理資料，標出缺漏或需要人工核對的項目。

交付產物 彙整表、異常註記與可回查的資料來源。

人工決策與授權 付款、報稅與財務判斷由指定人員負責，不以 AI 輸出直接執行。

維運與資安 AI Agent 組合

## 建立可追溯的維運管理流程。

能力範圍 依核准範圍做例行檢查，將異常、變更與驗證結果接成待辦。

交付產物 巡檢摘要、變更紀錄、異常與復原檢查表。

人工決策與授權 正式系統變更先登記，權限依需求開放；守衛查驗證據後再確認完成。

VALIDATE BEFORE SCALE

## 依驗證結果，評估規模化。

先定義資料輸入、產物規格、覆核責任與禁止操作，再以情境驗收確認適用範圍。跨部門擴充（Scale）以既有流程的驗證結果及維運能力為前提，設備與模型同步評估。

展開 AI 導入規劃。

ABOUT THINK BIG

Think BIG（大想成業有限公司）是總部位於台灣、服務全球的企業 AI Agent 導入商。我們從守護企業資安出發，以 TB FRAME（我們的四階段導入方法：評估、建置、驗證、維運）把 AI Agent 建在公司自己的環境裡（公司設備，或公司名下的雲端主機），並提供一年陪跑維運。選地端版時，模型與文件都在公司設備內處理；選雲端輔助版時，問題與檢索到的文件段落會送到模型廠商處理。我們扮演企業的遠端 FDE（Forward Deployed Engineer，前沿部署工程師）團隊：從聽懂需求、建置知識庫與 AI Agent、上線，到後續維運，一手包辦；另有個人 AI 助理安裝方案。

地端部署不等於所有連線都在本機。若使用雲端模型或外部服務，相關請求仍會送出；需要資料不出公司時，須確認本機模型、外連限制與可用功能。

FUNCTIONAL CAPABILITIES

## 將部門需求，
轉化為可驗收的能力。

將工作需求拆解為可描述的輸入、執行步驟與產物，並將人工核准納入流程設計。

MARKETING / 行銷

### 內容製作缺乏一致的知識基礎。

AI AGENT / 能力範圍

### 整合核准素材，產出可編修的內容草稿。

交付與驗收：內容草稿與待確認項目。對外行動須經指定負責人核准。

CUSTOMER SERVICE / 客服

### 重複查詢增加客服處理負擔。

AI AGENT / 能力範圍

### 依知識依據準備回覆，例外情境交由人工處理。

交付與驗收：回覆草稿與待人工處理清單。對外行動須經指定負責人核准。

SALES OPERATIONS / 業務

### 詢問紀錄與後續追蹤缺乏整合。

AI AGENT / 能力範圍

### 彙整需求脈絡，建立可追蹤的業務待辦。

交付與驗收：詢問摘要與追蹤清單。對外行動須經指定負責人核准。

FINANCE OPERATIONS / 財務

### 報表彙整與差異核對依賴人工。

AI AGENT / 能力範圍

### 依授權彙整資料，提供來源與差異核對清單。

交付與驗收：彙整報表與差異清單。對外行動須經指定負責人核准。

PRICING / 方案定價

## 公司導入 AI，
依需求報價

三種方案，清楚定義範圍與交付天數，都含第一年維護服務；AI 模型費用由客戶自備。實際內容與報價依需求訪談確認。

STARTER / 入門級

入門方案

依需求報價｜付款分兩次：簽約 50%、驗收通過 50%

員工直接問公司的 SOP 和規章。知識庫最多 30 份文件，AI 依文件回答、附出處；沒有依據就交回人確認。

BEST FOR
5–20 人的店家、工作室、門市，文件幾十份，讓員工或客人查 SOP、價目、常見問題。（醫療院所請改評估標準方案以上）

- 知識庫：1 個，≤30 份、≤300 頁、≤50 MB

- 通路：LINE 官方帳號或網頁嵌入，二選一

- 使用人數：不限

- 教學影片 1–2 支 + 快速手冊

- 首年維護：異常排查、缺陷修正、安全修補、監控

- 回覆時效：工作日 1 個工作日內真人回覆

- 首年文件更新：1 次（≤20 份）

- 交付天數：範圍凍結與資料到位後 30 天內

第二年選配續約費用依報價（含稅）。由客戶決定是否續約，不自動扣款。

STANDARD
STANDARD / 標準級

標準方案

依需求報價｜付款分兩次：簽約 50%、驗收通過 50%

回答問題，也幫忙打草稿。文件最多 100 份，還能處理試算表，並新增一項工作草稿任務（詢問摘要、回覆草稿或表單摘要三選一）。

BEST FOR
10–50 人的中小公司，文件上百份，每天有重複的文書工作要整理或擬稿。

- 知識庫：1 個，≤100 份、≤1,000 頁、≤200 MB + 試算表

- 工作草稿任務：1 項（三選一）

- 通路：LINE、網頁或內部通訊工具，三選一

- 使用人數：不限

- 教學影片 2–3 支 + 操作手冊

- 首年維護：全含（同入門級）

- 回覆時效：工作日 1 個工作日內真人回覆

- 首年文件更新：每半年 1 次，共 2 次（每次 ≤50 份）

- 交付天數：範圍凍結與資料到位後 30 天內

第二年選配續約費用依報價（含稅）。由客戶決定是否續約，不自動扣款。

COMPLETE / 完整級

完整方案

依需求報價｜付款分兩次：簽約 50%、驗收通過 50%

回答、打草稿，文件還會自動同步。額外包含一個唯讀串接（例如雲端硬碟資料夾自動同步），以及可加購擴充包。

BEST FOR
20–100 人，文件常更新且放在雲端硬碟，希望 AI 自動同步、不用人工上傳，之後可能加購大量知識庫或表格查詢。

- 知識庫：1 個，≤100 份、≤1,000 頁、≤200 MB + 試算表

- 工作草稿任務：1 項（三選一）

- 唯讀串接：1 個（例如雲端硬碟自動同步）

- 通路：LINE、網頁或內部通訊工具，三選一

- 使用人數：不限

- 教學影片 3–5 支 + 完整操作手冊

- 首年維護：全含，每月 1 小時操作諮詢

- 首年文件更新：每季 1 次，共 4 次（每次 ≤50 份）

- 交付天數：範圍凍結與資料到位後 30 天內

- 可加購擴充包

第二年選配續約費用依報價（含稅）。由客戶決定是否續約，不自動扣款。

### 三種方案共同條件

- 使用人數不限（效能取決於客戶設備規格）

- AI 模型費用由客戶自備，TB 不代墊、不轉售。可選地端版（模型裝在公司設備，資料在公司內處理）或雲端輔助版（用公司自己的帳號向模型廠商申請 API，問題與檢索到的文件段落會送到模型廠商處理）

- 客戶自備一台 24 小時開機的電腦；選雲端輔助版時也可用雲端主機

- 簽約前先做遠端設備預檢，裝不起來就不簽，客戶不會付到錢

- 三種方案首年內均可補差價升級：預約訪談了解升級條件

首年內補差價升級，前面付過的錢不會浪費。擴充包（進階功能）僅限完整級加購。

[填問卷，看看哪種方案適合我 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/start/)
[預約 15 分鐘線上評估 ›](https://lin.ee/n5KW430)

DATA SOVEREIGNTY

## 以資料政策，
決定部署架構。

資料主權（Data Sovereignty）落實於處理位置、存取權限與外部傳送規則。依企業政策與設備條件選擇配置，並逐項驗證串接相容性。

### 地端版

模型與指定資料在公司設備內處理。若要求資料不外傳，也要一起核對日誌、備份及外部串接。

### 雲端輔助版

使用雲端模型時，問題與檢索到的文件段落會送到模型廠商處理，適用該廠商的服務條款。導入前先列出傳送欄位、用途、帳號權限與費用，確認授權後才納入流程。

支援技術：OpenClaw、Claude、MCP、RAG。串接與更換模型需確認相容性，並重新驗證工作結果。

OPERATING MODEL

## 工具能力之外，
明確界定營運責任。

營運模型（Operating Model）定義工具由誰配置、變更由誰核准、產物如何驗收，以及問題由誰追蹤。

「一般 AI 工具」指自行訂閱、由企業自行設定與維護的常見使用方式；各產品能力依實際方案而異。

PROCUREMENT FAQ

## 釐清導入條件，
支持企業採購決策。

從資料處理、服務邊界到維運責任，提供導入評估與採購討論所需的基本依據。

如何評選 AI 導入服務商？

評選應涵蓋流程適配、資料治理、交付驗收及持續維運。要求服務商明列工作範圍、存取權限、驗收條件與問題處理責任。Think BIG 以實際運作的 AI 團隊治理流程說明能力，不展示客戶身分或資料。

地端部署如何落實資料主權？

地端配置將工作資料與執行環境部署於企業指定設備。使用雲端模型或外部服務時，須另行確認傳送欄位、用途與授權。要求資料不出公司，仍需核對本機模型、外連限制、日誌及備份配置。選雲端輔助版時，問題與檢索到的文件段落會送到模型廠商處理，適用該廠商的服務條款。

導入適用性是否取決於企業規模？

適用性主要取決於流程可定義程度、資料可用性與驗收責任。可先界定單一工作流程進行評估，再依驗證結果規劃擴充；僅需個人助理的需求另有個人方案。

導入進度如何規劃與管理？

TB FRAME 以評估定義、架構建置、驗證交付與治理維運四階段管理導入。進度依工作範圍、資料整備、系統權限及驗收條件共同確認，以階段交付物追蹤；三種方案於範圍凍結與資料到位後 30 天內交付。

企業方案有哪些級距？

企業方案依需求報價，請[預約需求訪談](https://thinkbigtw.com/contact/)取得正式報價。三種方案（入門／標準／完整）均含建置、教學影片與第一年維護服務。首年內均可補差價升級。第二年選配續約，由客戶自己決定是否續約，不自動扣款。

企業服務如何界定報價範圍？

三種方案都是清楚定義的範圍，不另外個別報價。超出方案範圍的需求（例如自動對客人回覆、寫回 ERP、大量串接）另案洽詢。導入服務、AI 模型費用由客戶自備分項說明，供企業確認採購範圍與後續成本。

TB CONTINUITY（AI Agent 年度治理與維運）包含哪些維運責任？

TB CONTINUITY｜AI Agent 年度治理與維運，提供一年陪跑，涵蓋約定範圍內的問題追蹤、維護檢查、變更紀錄與使用調整。服務窗口、責任邊界及新增需求處理方式於合約中確認。

AI Agent 的自主操作權限如何控管？

依最小權限原則配置資料與操作範圍。對外發送、花費及正式系統異動須經指定負責人核准；AI Agent 提供工作產物與執行證據，人員保留關鍵決策權。

既有工具與模型能否持續沿用？

先盤點既有系統介面、帳號權限與相容性，再評估整合範圍。更換模型時須重新驗證流程與輸出品質，既有配置能否沿用依實際測試結果確認。

# 以交付紀律，
建立可治理的 AI 流程。

TB FRAME 是 Think BIG 的 AI Agent 導入方法論，分為 Assess 評估定義、Build 架構建置、Validate 驗證交付、Operate 治理維運四個階段，每階段列明交付物與覆核責任。

- 01

ASSESS

### 評估定義

交付物 流程盤點、資料清單、優先序與驗收基準。

- 02

BUILD

### 架構建置

交付物 部署配置、角色權限與可操作的 AI Agent 流程。

- 03

VALIDATE

### 驗證交付

交付物 情境測試、例外處理紀錄與操作交接文件。

交付物 一年陪跑、維護紀錄、變更驗證與改善待辦。

TB FRAME

## 每一步，
都有交付依據。

評估、建置、驗證、維運。
將治理落實於完整導入流程。

- 01 Assess

- 02 Build

- 03 Validate

- 04 Operate

01 / ASSESS

## 評估定義：確立範圍與驗收基準。

階段交付物 流程圖、資料與權限清單、優先順序、驗收條件。

決策與覆核責任 企業確認業務目標與資料授權；TB 明列可實施範圍、先備條件與排除項目。

02 / BUILD

## 架構建置：整合資料、權限與執行環境。

階段交付物 部署與配置說明、串接項目、可操作的 AI Agent 流程。

決策與覆核責任 共同確認地端與外部服務界線、存取權限及使用成本，配置變更納入事前登記。

03 / VALIDATE

## 驗證交付：核對產物與例外處理。

階段交付物 正常與例外情境的測試紀錄、操作說明、問題回報窗口。

決策與覆核責任 由指定負責人核對產物，驗證無依據、資料缺漏、未授權操作及服務中斷的處理機制。

04 / OPERATE

## 治理維運：持續管理問題與變更。

階段交付物 維護與變更紀錄、問題追蹤、改善待辦、必要的操作說明更新。

決策與覆核責任 透過 TB CONTINUITY（導入後一年的維護、問題追蹤與使用調整）  年度治理與維運，於約定中明列維護範圍、第三方費用、擴充需求及終止交接責任。

# 什麼是 RAG？讓 AI 依公司文件回答｜Think BIG

COMPANY KNOWLEDGE / RAG

# 什麼是 RAG？
讓 AI 依公司文件回答

RAG（Retrieval-Augmented Generation，檢索增強生成）是一種讓 AI 回答前，先從指定的公司文件或知識庫找出相關段落，再依據這些內容生成回答的方法。系統可一併提供引用出處，讓人回查答案依據。回答品質仍取決於文件內容、檢索結果與驗證方式，不能只因使用 RAG 就視為正確。

Think BIG 編輯部 · 2026 年 9 月 27 日

- 01

## 確認可讀範圍

先核對提問者身分與文件權限。

- 02

## 找出相關段落

從核准文件檢索可用的回答依據。

- 03

## 回答並附出處

讓人回查；依據不足時轉人工。

常見問題

## RAG 和一般聊天 AI 差在哪？

未接入指定文件的聊天 AI，主要依模型既有知識與當次對話內容回答。RAG 在生成答案前多了檢索步驟，讓回答能參考公司核准的制度、產品文件或操作說明。聊天介面本身也可能使用 RAG，差別在有沒有檢索指定資料，而不是介面長什麼樣。

例如問「這項服務包含哪些支援？」時，RAG 可先找到目前有效的服務說明，再整理回答並附上段落來源。找不到適用版本，就應說明缺少依據，交由人員確認。

## RAG 和微調（fine-tuning）差在哪？

RAG 著重回答時要參考哪些資料，更新文件與索引通常不必重新訓練生成模型。微調則使用訓練範例調整模型參數，常用來改善特定任務、回覆格式或表達方式。兩者可以搭配；微調不會自動提供文件引用，也不能代替即時的權限檢查。

若重點是經常更新的公司知識與可回查來源，可先評估 RAG；若重點是穩定的輸出格式或任務行為，再用測試結果判斷是否需要微調。

## 企業導入 RAG 要準備什麼資料？

先選一個要回答的業務範圍，整理經核准的常見問題、服務規範、產品說明與作業流程。資料要能讀取文字；掃描檔須先辨識並校對。每份文件應有負責人、有效日期、版本、可存取角色與來源位置。

- 保留文件標題、段落關係與表格欄位，讓切段後的內容仍有足夠上下文。

- 移除重複、過期及無授權的內容，訂出更新與撤回流程。

- 準備代表性問題與預期依據，包含資料缺漏、權限不足及容易混淆的情境。

## 使用 RAG，資料會不會外流？

RAG 是回答方法，不是資料安全承諾。資料會傳到哪裡，要看文件儲存、檢索、文字轉換、模型推論、日誌與備份各在哪裡處理，以及連接哪些外部服務。

地端部署不等於所有連線都在本機。即使知識庫在公司內，使用雲端模型時，問題與檢索出的段落仍可能送往外部；雲端文字轉換或索引服務也要列入資料流向。若要求資料不出公司，須一併確認本機模型、檢索與資料處理配置、外連限制、日誌及備份。

權限須在檢索與取回內容時落實，不能只在提示詞寫「不要透露」。採用外部服務前，應確認傳送欄位、用途、保留政策及授權，詳見 [Think BIG 資安與治理](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/)與[地端 AI 與資料主權](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/local-ai-data/)。

## 怎麼驗收 RAG 回答是否正確？

先由熟悉業務的人建立測試問題、正確依據與可接受的回答範圍，再逐題核對檢索段落與最終回答。引用出處要能打開，而且確實支持結論；有引用不等於回答一定正確。

- 一般問題：是否找對文件版本，答案有沒有超出文件內容。

- 無法回答：沒有相關內容或文件互相矛盾時，能否明確說明不足並轉人工。

- 權限邊界：未授權的使用者能否被擋下，回答與引用是否都沒有洩漏受限內容。

- 更新與例外：文件撤回、索引更新或服務中斷後，系統是否依約定停止或轉人工。

留下測試結果、失敗原因與修正紀錄，文件或配置更動後重測。驗收門檻由雙方依流程確認，參考[AI Agent 驗收框架](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/ai-acceptance/)。

## RAG 常見的失敗原因有哪些？

文件過期或互相矛盾 AI 可能依舊規則作答。指定文件負責人、有效版本與更新頻率，撤回舊內容時同步更新索引。

權限沒有分清楚 共用知識庫可能把受限段落交給不該看到的人。依角色檢查可讀範圍，連引用來源也要套用權限。

切段不當，找不到完整依據 段落太碎會遺失條件；太長會混入無關內容。依文件結構切段、保留標題與版本資訊，並用實際問題驗證檢索結果。

掃描辨識錯誤、問題描述模糊、只測容易的題目，也會掩蓋缺陷。應分開檢查「有沒有找到對的段落」和「回答有沒有忠於段落」。

## Think BIG 如何把 RAG 用在客服 AI Agent？

Think BIG 的客服知識流程先以核准的服務與治理文件界定可回答範圍，再找出相關內容準備回覆草稿；沒有依據的問題整理成待確認清單，交由人員補充。RAG 用於企業知識問答時，也沿用這個原則：先確認來源與權限，再檢索、附上可回查依據並驗證回答。

承諾、退款與爭議由人員決定；對外發送、花費及正式系統異動仍需指定負責人核准。實際是否採用向量檢索、其他檢索方式或混合配置，依文件規模、資料政策與情境測試確認，不把所有知識查詢都稱為同一種實作。

同樣的方式可用於業務查詢核准的產品資料，或讓行銷核對品牌文件。先讓單一流程的回答與例外處理可驗證，再評估擴充。可查看[客服 AI Agent 的能力與人工責任](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/departments/#service)。

Think BIG（大想成業有限公司）是總部位於台灣、服務全球的企業 AI Agent 導入商。我們從守護企業資安出發，以 TB FRAME（我們的四階段導入方法：評估、建置、驗證、維運）把 AI Agent 建在公司自己的環境裡（公司設備，或公司名下的雲端主機），並提供一年陪跑維運。選地端版時，模型與文件都在公司設備內處理；選雲端輔助版時，問題與檢索到的文件段落會送到模型廠商處理。我們扮演企業的遠端 FDE（Forward Deployed Engineer，前沿部署工程師）團隊：從聽懂需求、建置知識庫與 AI Agent、上線，到後續維運，一手包辦；另有個人 AI 助理安裝方案。

## 延伸閱讀與技術來源

RAG 的技術概念可參考 [Lewis 等人的原始論文：Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)。本站的資料與權限說明依 [Think BIG 資安承諾](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/)整理；文件準備與驗收項目是本文的導入建議。

YOUR NEXT STORE MANAGER

## 同樣 72 萬。
不同的下一步。

A 店 / 來客減少 先看人流 ↗

B 店 / 成交下降 先看接待 ↗

團隊把線索變成行動。

互動模擬 / 示範數據

01 / 選情境，再看結果

## 今天，你想先看哪一家店？

以下為等長兩期的模擬資料。也可以修改數字，觀察分析如何改變。

02 / 從數據到行動

### 準備好看看數字背後的線索？

選擇案例，按下「產出診斷與行動清單」，即可取得營收拆解、待確認問題與三項行動。

03 / 與 AI 討論下一步

## 不只看數字，還能接著問。

例如：「如果不能增加廣告預算，這週能先做什麼？」AI 會參考上方目前的數據與你的補充，提供分析或追問。

HOW IT WORKS

## 每個結論，都有依據。

01 / 計算

### 先看營收結構

營收＝來客數 × 成交率 × 客單價。達成率＝本期營收 ÷ 本期目標。

02 / 找線索

### 分開事實與推測

依來客 → 成交 → 客單的順序拆解營收變動。數據能定位變動，無法單獨證明原因。

03 / 安排行動

### 帶著問題回到現場

產出待確認問題、負責角色與追蹤指標；一週後回看結果，再調整做法。

MAKE IT REAL.

# 常見問題｜Think BIG

THINK BIG

# 常見問題

彙整個人安裝、企業導入、維運與資料權限的常見問題。

企業導入

## 企業如何報價？

企業方案依需求報價。三種方案（入門／標準／完整）都含建置、教學影片與第一年維護服務。付款分兩次：簽約 50%、驗收通過 50%。第二年選配續約，由客戶決定是否續約，不自動扣款。AI 模型費用由客戶自備。請[預約需求訪談取得報價](https://thinkbigtw.com/contact/)。

[查看方案比較 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/#packages)

個人方案

## 個人安裝有哪些選擇？

個人方案主打本地大模型 AI Agent 搭建，把 AI 模型和 AI Agent 一起裝在你的電腦上；電腦規格不夠可改搭雲端大模型，同方案、同價格。方案含：人格版 AI 助理（討好型或討伐型）、雙 AI Agent（共存版或含記憶互通）、年約。個人方案請至蝦皮賣場選購（[thinkbigtw 蝦皮賣場](https://shopee.tw/shop/105010395)），或預約需求訪談取得報價。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/pricing/personal/)

支援期

## 人格版與雙 AI Agent 方案包含多久支援？

人格版 AI 助理含 7 天技術諮詢；雙 AI Agent 共存版含 7 天技術諮詢；雙 AI Agent（含記憶互通）含 2 小時線上技術導覽＋安裝後 7 天技術諮詢。兩者均無年度維運承諾，需要長期顧請看年約。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/pricing/personal/#tier2)

年度維運

## 年約如何續約？

個人年約次年可選配續約，含每週維護。年約的 48 小時故障修復承諾僅適用個人年約約定範圍。續約費用依需求報價，請見個人方案頁。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/pricing/personal/#tier3)

安裝流程

## 下單後什麼時候安裝？

下單後預約遠端安裝時間，由工程師透過 AnyDesk／DeskIn 協助。設備、帳號與需要的功能會先確認。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/pricing/personal/)

資料權限

## 遠端安裝會看到我的資料嗎？

工程師會操作客戶電腦，可能看到畫面上的工作資料或敏感資訊。依最小權限與確認範圍操作，客戶在場，可先關閉無關文件；安裝後可中止連線並移除遠端權限。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/#remote-install)

模型費用

## 價格包含 AI 模型用量費嗎？

本地版模型運算不另收用量費。改搭雲端大模型時，API Key 由你本人申請，模型使用費依用量向模型廠商計費（工程師提供引導）；coding agent 訂閱與所需第三方帳號請自行準備。

[查看方案範圍 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/pricing/personal/)

退款

## 安裝失敗怎麼辦？

人格版 AI 助理若因我方技術問題無法完成安裝，全額退費；其他服務的退款、驗收與變更依服務條款及雙方確認內容辦理。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/pricing/personal/#tier1)

資料流向

## 裝在自己電腦上，資料就不會外傳嗎？

地端部署不等於所有連線都在本機。若使用雲端模型、通訊平台或外部服務，相關請求仍會送出；需確認本機模型、外連限制、日誌與備份。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/trust/)

諮詢摘要

## AI 顧問如何保存諮詢資料？

諮詢摘要與聯絡資料，經你確認送出後保存至你請求刪除為止；聊天逐字稿不隨摘要保存，聯絡資料不送入模型。來信 AI@thinkbigtw.com 或透過 LINE 官方帳號請求刪除，14 天內回覆。

[查看完整說明 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/privacy.html#ai-inquiry)

AI Agent 市場

## 新的 AI Agent 出來了，還需要龍蝦（OpenClaw）嗎？

兩者擅長的工作不同，可以一起用。常見的大模型品牌 AI Agent 有 Grok Bot（xAI）、Claude（Anthropic）、ChatGPT Agent 與 dots（OpenAI）、Gemini Spark（Google）、Muse（Meta）等，每一個都很好。但如果要長時間運作、又想費用可控，大模型品牌推出的 AI Agent 就不會是首選，但很適合拿來協作。OpenClaw（龍蝦）等開源 AI Agent 可自選模型、依用量付費、24 小時常駐，適合長時間例行運作。

[各家 AI Agent 一次看懂 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/guides/ai-agents/)

資安

## 你們裝的 AI Agent 跟大品牌的有什麼不一樣？資安怎麼顧？

資安沒有人能打包票。我們做的，就是一道一道的審查。技能裝進去之前先掃描；固定版本、不自動更新；上線前先過資安審查；金鑰只放系統設定檔、不在聊天裡傳。

# 全 Agent 串接 | Think BIG!

個人 AI 助理

# 全 Agent 串接

你已經在付 Claude Code／Codex 的訂閱費了——讓它們組成一個團隊。

Multi-Agent Orchestration（多代理協作）：讓 OpenClaw 和你既有的 coding agent（Claude Code／Codex／Antigravity 等）進駐同一個「協作會議室」分工做事。OpenClaw 負責接指令與日常任務，coding agent 負責寫程式、改檔案、跑測試——這是 2026 年 Anthropic、Google、Microsoft 都在推的架構方向。

## 你是不是每天都在——

- 開著 Claude Code、又開著 ChatGPT、又開著別的工具，自己當人肉轉接頭？

- 付了 coding agent 訂閱費，卻只有坐在電腦前打指令的時候用得到？

- 出門在外想派工給 AI，只能等回到電腦前？

## 怎麼運行

1

收到 你打開專屬會議室網址（可加到手機主畫面當 App），下一道指令

2

判斷 OpenClaw 分析任務，決定自己做還是派給 coding agent

3

執行 多個 Agent 在會議室裡分工協作，你可即時看到協作過程

4

回報 最終結果報告自動推播到你指定的通訊軟體

會議室建在你自己免費註冊的 Supabase 專案上，資料與其他客戶天然隔離。

## 你得到什麼

- OpenClaw 官方最新版＋ 60 組全客製技能 （依你的職業量身開發）

- Coding Agent 串接（Claude Code／Codex／Antigravity 等，需自備訂閱）

- 跨 Agent 協作會議室＋結果推播通訊軟體

- 手機下指令、電腦上的 Agent 團隊接力完成——不必人在電腦前

- 2 小時線上技術導覽＋安裝後 7 天 技術諮詢

- 服務費依需求報價，無月費 （指我方服務費），請至[蝦皮賣場](https://shopee.tw/shop/105010395)選購

想要會學習的第二顆大腦？→ [看「雙 AI Agent」](https://thinkbigtw.com/dual-agent/)。

方案價格

# AI Agent 驗收框架｜成果、例外與授權｜Think BIG

ENTERPRISE INSIGHTS

# AI Agent 驗收框架：成果、例外與授權

以輸入條件、產物規格、例外處理與核准機制建立驗收框架，並將驗證紀錄納入後續變更管理。

IN THIS ARTICLE

## 將業務目標轉為驗收條件

將工作目標轉為可核對的產物規格，包括輸出格式、必要欄位、資料來源及覆核角色。例如回覆草稿應附依據，彙整表應列示缺漏；以可檢查的條件取代概括性效益敘述。

## 涵蓋正常、異常與未授權情境

準備資料完整、無法查證、欄位缺漏、服務中斷與權限不足等情境。驗證 AI 是否如實回報、停止未授權操作，並依約定程序交由指定人員處理。

## 建立可回查的測試證據

記錄測試條件、配置、輸入範圍、預期與實際結果，使驗收結論可回查。敏感資料的保留及存取須另行約定，測試紀錄不應任意複製完整原始資料。

## 將人工核准納入驗收範圍

人機協作（Human-in-the-loop）須有可驗證的控制點。對必須核准的步驟，確認系統在未獲授權前停止執行；技術上可自動完成，並不代表業務上已獲授權。

## 針對變更執行影響範圍驗證

模型、資料與權限調整均可能影響輸出。依 TB FRAME（我們的四階段導入方法：評估、建置、驗證、維運）  的治理維運階段，先登記變更範圍、影響與復原方式，再以相關情境驗證結果，將驗收延伸至持續營運。

Think BIG 編輯部 · 2026 年 9 月 26 日

[使用 AI 導入規劃工作表 ›](https://thinkbigtw.com/enterprise/process/worksheet/)

## 以明確的業務需求，
展開 AI 導入規劃。
